public_rationale: Marcus firmly predicts eventual AGI but only tentatively suggests the next decade. The reviewed announcements and evaluations do not establish a decisive event under the stated rule. Contemporary coverage still describes the achievement as disputed. An unresolved achievement claim cannot settle this forecast, and continued non-arrival cannot falsify an unlimited prediction.
limitations: Broad acceptance is an evaluator-supplied interpretation of the undefined term AGI.
The search cannot establish that no qualifying system exists anywhere.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AGI will eventually come, possibly within the next decade.
conditions: eventually; maybe in the next decade

statement.excerpt: And AGI—hopefully safe, trustworthy AGI– will eventually come. Maybe in the next decade.

our_interpretation: The firm prediction is eventual arrival. 'Maybe' does not establish a deadline, and 'hopefully' expresses a wish rather than a condition.
I read AGI as broadly human-level cognitive competence across domains, demonstrated independently and widely accepted as general intelligence. Marcus supplies no operational test.
criteria.support_condition: A publicly demonstrated system receives independent evaluation and broad acceptance as AGI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that AGI cannot ever be built. Continued non-arrival over any finite period is insufficient.
